 Bob Heinz's Obituary
 Bob Heinz, a beloved husband, father, and grandfather, passed away on Saturday, October 31, 2026, in Fresno, California . He was 79.
Born on July 25, 1947, in Wisconsin to Ken and Bette Heinz, Bob grew up in a large family near Milwaukee before moving to California during his high school years. He graduated from Lincoln High School in Stockton, where he excelled in football, basketball, and track and field. He continued his education and football career at the University of the Pacific, where he met Carol Covington, his future wife of 56 years.
A defensive tackle for the UOP Tigers, Bob was drafted by the Miami Dolphins in 1969 and went on to play ten seasons in the NFL. Wearing #72, Bob was a member of the “No-Name Defense” and a starter on the only undefeated team in NFL history, winning back-to-back championships in Super Bowls VII and VIII.
Bob and Carol married in 1970 and raised their three children in Menlo Park, California , their home for many years. After retiring from a long career in sales, the couple relocated to Fresno to be near family. Family was Bob’s greatest source of pride and happiness. He will be remembered for his friendship, his sense of humor, and his deep love for those closest to him. He enjoyed a good cigar and bourbon, the music of Jimmy Buffett, cheering on the San Francisco Giants, and rooting against any NFL team attempting perfection.
Bob is survived by his wife, Carol; his children, Julie, Joe, and John; daughter-in-law, Laura; grandchildren, Matthew and Samantha; sister-in-law, Claire Covington; and his nieces and nephews, all of whom he loved dearly. He was preceded in death by his parents and his siblings, Mike, Pete, Geoff, Peggy (Sain), and Doug.
A private family service is planned. In lieu of flowers, donations may be made in Bob’s memory to the Miami Dolphins Foundation.
